concepts.why: The patient presented with classic symptoms of appendicitis, including abdominal pain that localized to the right lower quadrant, nausea, and a positive Rovsing sign, and imaging studies showed inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve.
The patient has a history of endometriosis and the biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis.
The patient developed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass.
The appendix was not identified on imaging studies, leading to a presumptive diagnosis of inverted appendix.
The patient has a pericecal soft-tissue mass that could be a neoplasm, and the differential diagnosis included neoplasm.
The patient has inflammation and a soft-tissue mass adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve, which could be a pericecal abscess.
The patient has endometriosis and the biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis in the intestine.
The patient has mild inflammatory changes of the terminal ileum, which could be acute ileitis.
The patient has small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, which could be due to a stricture.
The patient has inflammation of the terminal ileum, which could be terminal ileitis.

rationales.F01: The fact of intermittent throbbing abdominal pain is neutral for all concepts as it is a non-specific symptom.
rationales.F02: The fact that the pain began periumbilically and localized to the right lower quadrant is moderately suggestive of acute appendicitis and inverted appendix.
rationales.F04: The fact of moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant is moderately suggestive of acute appendicitis, inverted appendix, and pericecal abscess.
rationales.F07: The fact of lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve is strongly suggestive of acute appendicitis and pericecal abscess.
rationales.F08: The fact that the appendix was not identified is strongly against acute appendicitis but suggests inverted appendix.
rationales.F10: The fact of biopsy demonstrating acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis is strongly suggestive of endometriosis and intestinal endometriosis.
rationales.F12: The fact of small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum is strongly suggestive of small-bowel obstruction and pericecal abscess.
